tldr: Anthropic expanded Claude Cowork to web and mobile on Jul 7, publishing its own analysis of the everyday tasks people delegate to it most. A week of internal use-case posts followed, showing how Anthropic's own marketing team automates reporting with it and how to pair it with Claude Fable 5 for long, complex work.
whats_new: Anthropic detailed for the first time how it technically contains Claude across Cowork, Code, and web — arguing agent safety depends on deterministic filesystem, network, and execution limits, not model judgment alone.
why_it_matters: Cowork is Anthropic's async, hand-off-and-walk-away agent product — this containment-architecture disclosure is the first concrete answer to the platform-engineer question of what actually stops an unsupervised agent from doing damage while you're away.

status.state: Expanding · usage patterns, use cases, and containment architecture disclosed
status.detail: Cowork rolled out to web/mobile on Jul 7 with Anthropic's own usage analysis; a week of use-case posts followed (marketing-ops automation, pairing with Claude Fable 5); Jul 22 brought the first detailed look at the containment architecture — filesystem, network, and execution limits — that Anthropic says agent safety depends on.

beats.headline: Claude Cowork expands to web and mobile, with Anthropic's own usage analysis
beats.summary: Anthropic ships Cowork to web and mobile — hand off a task, close the laptop, keep working — alongside an analysis of the everyday tasks people delegate to it most.

beats.headline: Anthropic's own teams show how they use Cowork
beats.summary: Anthropic's marketing operations team details automating reporting and campaign builds with Cowork, then Anthropic publishes guidance on pairing it with Claude Fable 5 for long, complex work.

beats.headline: Anthropic details the containment architecture behind Claude's agent safety
beats.summary: InfoQ reports Anthropic's account of how it places deterministic limits on Claude's filesystem, network, and execution environment across web, Code, and Cowork — a technical answer to what actually contains an unsupervised agent.

open_questions: What specific containment mechanisms — sandboxing, permission scopes, network egress rules — does Anthropic enforce by default in Cowork, versus what's opt-in?
Does the containment architecture change how much unattended, multi-step work a team can safely hand to Cowork, or is it primarily a trust-building message?
Do Claude Code and the web app share the same containment primitives Anthropic describes for Cowork, or does each surface implement its own limits?
take_for_builders: Before handing Cowork an unattended, multi-step task, check what filesystem, network, and execution limits Anthropic actually enforces by default versus what you need to configure yourself.
